stem.en: An election is held on time, but each case below reduces its democratic value. Sort each case by what has failed.

text.en: Candidates are influenced by personal favours
An officer on duty favours one candidate over the others
Totals are added up wrongly and no one checks them
A voter in a wheelchair cannot get into the polling station
A voter who cannot see finds no Braille at the machine

explanation.en: Favours mean the process is not impartial. A wrong count means the result cannot be trusted. A voter who cannot reach or use the booth has been left out, so the process is not inclusive.

hints.en: Ask of each case: was someone favoured, was the count wrong, or was a voter left out?
